native_result.query: In which domain did both original and replication studies primarily use student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%)?
native_result.HypoA: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).
native_result.HypoB: The domain in which both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects is the Social discipline (social psychology). Among the 74 Social-discipline studies, original studies used student subjects in 83.8% (62/74) and replications in 81.1% (60/74) — the closest match to the cited 82.4%/80.9% — and Social is the only domain where both original and replication are majority-student under every tested analysis scheme (Cognitive: 75.5%/81.6% study-level; Economics: 94.4%/100.0%).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927 rows, 57 cols, 141 unique O/R-pair ids). Verified key fields: discipline (Social 668/Cognitive 241/Economics 18), subjects.o (students 737/anyone 143/community 46/1 NaN), subjects.r (students 744/online 148/community 25/anyone 9/1 NaN); no case/whitespace variants, no full-row or (id,lab_id) duplicates; single missing-subjects row rpp.154 (drop=True). Built the main study-level frame (one row per id: aggregated=True pooled rows for ml1/ml3, single rows for rpp/ee) and computed per-discipline shares of 'students' for subjects.o and subjects.r, with missing counted in the denominator. Ran sensitivity analyses: missing excluded from denominator, row-level (927 lab/single rows), and drop==False subsets, and selected the domain minimizing distance to (82.4, 80.9). The second dataset (replication_success) was inspected and found unnecessary (no subjects/discipline columns). Executed script: analysis.py.

sub_hypo.text: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).
sub_hypo.context: Original and replication studies in Psychology.
sub_hypo.relations: Students were the predominant subject type in both original (82.4%) and replication (80.9%) studies. Community members accounted for 7.4% of original and 8.8% of replication studies; anyone accounted for 10.3% and 5.9%, respectively. Online participants accounted for 4.4% of replication studies.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).

sub_hypo.text: Social psychology is the discipline whose original and replication student-subject shares most closely match the cited 82.4% and 80.9%: among 74 Social studies, 62 originals (83.8%) and 60 replications (81.1%) used students.
sub_hypo.context: Original–replication study pairs in the meta-regression dataset, analyzed with one row per id: aggregated pooled rows for ml1/ml3 and single rows for rpp/ee, counting missing subjects in the denominator.
sub_hypo.relations: Per-discipline proportions using students in original and replication studies are compared with the target pair (82.4%, 80.9%); Social has the smallest distance. Study-level comparison shares are 75.5%/81.6% for Cognitive and 94.4%/100.0% for Economics.

sub_hypo.text: Social is the only discipline where both original and replication studies are majority-student under every tested analysis scheme.
sub_hypo.context: Original–replication studies across Social, Cognitive, and Economics, tested at the study level with missing subjects included or excluded from denominators, at the row level across 927 lab/single rows, and in drop==False subsets.
sub_hypo.relations: Only Social consistently has student-subject proportions greater than 50% for both originals and replications across all tested schemes.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The domain in which both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects is the Social discipline (social psychology). Among the 74 Social-discipline studies, original studies used student subjects in 83.8% (62/74) and replications in 81.1% (60/74) — the closest match to the cited 82.4%/80.9% — and Social is the only domain where both original and replication are majority-student under every tested analysis scheme (Cognitive: 75.5%/81.6% study-level; Economics: 94.4%/100.0%).
